reforms.description: The 1996 Budget reallocates C$ 260 million over three years towards technology and innovation, including the introduction of the Technology Partnerships Canada (TPC) programme to provide reimbursable financing to firms for close-to-market development of key technologies, aiming to enhance Canada's competitive edge.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The funding and support for technology development are expected to enhance competitiveness and innovation in the private sector.
reforms.status_evidence: The reforms were implemented as part of the 1996 Budget.
reforms.importance_rationale: The reforms involve significant funding and support mechanisms for technology development, but do not represent a structural overhaul.
reforms.source_quote: On the expenditure side, over the next three years spending of up to C$ 260 million will be reallocated in three structural-policy priority areas: education and employment opportunities for young Canadians; technology and innovation; and international trade.

reforms.description: The Internal Agreement on Trade includes a chapter aimed at improving inter-provincial labor mobility by eliminating barriers that prevent qualified workers from accessing employment opportunities across Canada.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Improving labor mobility is expected to enhance the efficiency of the labor market and support economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The reform was implemented as part of the Internal Agreement on Trade.
reforms.importance_rationale: The reform addresses significant barriers to labor mobility, which can have a meaningful impact on the labor market.
reforms.source_quote: The Agreement has a specific chapter dealing with labour mobility which aims to eliminate existing barriers that prevent a worker qualified for an occupation in one part of Canada having access to employment opportunities in that occupation elsewhere in the country.

reforms.description: The Canadian Technology Network (CTN) was launched to provide firms with quick and easy access to business expertise, advice, and information on technology, facilitating knowledge transfer and commercialization.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By providing access to expertise and information, the CTN supports firms in commercializing technology, which can enhance innovation and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The CTN was launched and is operational.
reforms.importance_rationale: The establishment of the CTN represents a significant initiative to improve access to technology-related business support.
reforms.source_quote: The Canadian Technology Network (CTN), a grouping of industry associations, research organisations, government institutes, and universities, was launched in 1996 to provide firms with quick and easy access to business expertise, advice and information on technology.

reforms.description: The Technology Partnerships Programme, a joint initiative of three Research Councils, aims to create partnerships among universities and SMEs for research development and commercialization.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By fostering partnerships between universities and SMEs, the programme is expected to enhance innovation and support the growth of the startup ecosystem.
reforms.status_evidence: The programme was announced but not yet implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: The initiative represents a significant effort to enhance collaboration between academia and industry.
reforms.source_quote: The Technology Partnerships Programme, a joint initiative of three Research Councils, aims to create partnerships among universities and SMEs for research development and commercialisation.
